subject: Mexican Revolution
hook: MEXICAN REVOLUTION IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The Mexican Revolution was essentially a decade‑long civil war, not just a popular uprising against Porfirio Díaz
angle_support: The revolutionary conflict was primarily a civil war, but foreign powers, having important economic and strategic interests in Mexico, figured in the outcome of Mexico's power struggles; U.S. involvement was particularly high.
The Revolution was a decade-long civil war, with new political leadership that gained power and legitimacy through their participation in revolutionary conflicts.
title: Why the Mexican Revolution Was Actually a 10-Year Civil War
description: Most summaries frame the Mexican Revolution as a simple fight to remove Porfirio Díaz. In reality, the dictator resigned within months, sparking a sprawling conflict between competing revolutionary factions. Here is how Mexico plunged into a decade of internal warfare.
narration: MEXICAN REVOLUTION IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a unified rebellion toppling an aging dictator. But Porfirio Díaz gave up power and fled after just six months. The actual fight had barely begun. Instead of peace, rival revolutionary armies turned on each other. Factions led by former allies battled for regional dominance and federal control until 1920, producing a catastrophic civil war that claimed nearly one million lives. Overthrowing the ruler was easy. Surviving the internal aftermath took a decade.
